text: 📸 Hospital General Regional IMSS — San Lorenzo Cacaotepec, Oaxaca, 2 de agosto de 2026

🇲🇽✊ "We are not building beds — we are reducing distances, waits, anguish and, above all, inequalities." "No estamos construyendo camas, estamos reduciendo distancias, esperas, angustias y, lo más importante, desigualdades." — Zoé Robledo, IMSS Director General, Oaxaca The new IMSS Regional General Hospital will have 530 beds, 57 specialties (neurosurgery, nuclear medicine, surgical oncology — firsts for IMSS Oaxaca), 42 hemodialysis machines and 2,826 health workers. This single hospital adds more beds than the IMSS built in Oaxaca in 36 years of neoliberal governments.

🇲🇽✊ Mexico is building a Universal Health Service — IMSS, ISSSTE and IMSS-Bienestar as one. "Our goal is that by the end of this administration, even if you belong to the IMSS, you can be treated for the main illnesses at the ISSSTE if it is closer, or at IMSS-Bienestar if it is closer." "Nuestro objetivo es que cuando termine el sexenio, aunque pertenezcas al IMSS, te puedas tratar para las principales enfermedades en el ISSSTE si te queda más cerca, o en el IMSS Bienestar si te queda más cerca." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, San Lorenzo Cacaotepec, Oaxaca She spoke at Ñuu Tata ("the town that heals" in Mixtec), a 50-hectare health city where three hospitals — ISSSTE (62% built), IMSS (first stone laid today) and a new IMSS-Bienestar hospital — will share specialists and services. 2 million seniors are already credentialed.

🇲🇽✊ "In its first 39 years, the IMSS built 27,000 hospital beds. In the next 36 years, only 4,000." "De 1943 al 2018, el IMSS construyó 27 mil camas en sus primeros 39 años. En sus siguientes 36 años solo se construyeron 4 mil camas." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, San Lorenzo Cacaotepec, Oaxaca Sheinbaum blamed 36 years of neoliberal governments (1982-2018) for the collapse of public health, as she laid the first stone of Oaxaca's new IMSS Regional General Hospital: 530 beds, 57 specialties, care for nearly 1 million people. Her government will build 9,000 hospital beds this sexenio.

🇲🇽✊ "I am proudly a housewife, a grandmother, a mother — and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces. Women can be whatever we want to be." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Tuxtepec, Oaxaca Sheinbaum recalled that on her first day in office, a TV comic sneered that "a housewife had arrived at the National Palace." She was announcing the Women's Wellbeing Pension: women aged 63-64 already receive it; registration for ages 60-62 opens in August, with automatic transfer to the universal pension at 65.

🚨🇲🇽 "Migrants are not criminals. They are honest, hardworking people — and they sustain the economy of the United States." "Without Mexicans there, the United States would not be what it is." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Tuxtepec, Oaxaca Speaking in Oaxaca's Cuenca del Papaloapan, where nearly every family has relatives across the border, Sheinbaum asked the crowd to tell them: "We protect them, we care for them. The Government of Mexico will always stand with our migrant brothers and sisters."

🇲🇽✊ "No luxuries, no privileges for rulers. The presidential plane was sold — and the sale built two hospitals." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Tuxtepec, Oaxaca Sheinbaum supervised the new IMSS Bienestar General Hospital in Tuxtepec, one of two hospitals funded by the sale of the presidential plane (the other is in Tlapa, Guerrero). Investment: 2.3 billion pesos; 150 beds; it will serve 1.2 million people in 109 municipalities of Oaxaca and Veracruz. Inauguration is set for August 4. She also announced 3 billion pesos to fix every operating room, hospital and clinic in Oaxaca.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>NEARSHORING IS LANDING: PLANT OPENINGS TRIPLE</u>

The nearshoring obituary was premature. New investment announcements fell nearly 80% in Q1 2026 as boardrooms wait out the T-MEC review — but inaugurations of previously committed plants are running at almost triple last year’s pace, Integralia analyst Alberto Quiroz told El Economista.

The corridor is clear: Querétaro and Guanajuato, up through San Luis Potosí to Nuevo León and Coahuila. Airbus opened a $35.8M plant in Querétaro, Clarios a $147M distribution center in Torreón, and Baltimore Aircoil its first Latin American factory in Nuevo León — $100M, 500 direct jobs.

The capital that was promised is arriving.

🇲🇽⚓ <u>211 NEW NAVAL OFFICERS — RECORD 73 WOMEN — SWORN TO DEFEND SOVEREIGNTY</u>

President Sheinbaum presided over the graduation of 211 naval engineer officers at the Heroica Escuela Naval Militar in Alvarado, Veracruz — the 2022-2026 class, with a record 73 women among them.

"Mexico believes in you, Mexico trusts in you, Mexico knows that when it needs you, you will be there — as the sailors of our homeland have always been," she told the new guardiamarinas, who carry "the responsibility of defending sovereignty, protecting Mexicans and honoring the homeland with values."

🇲🇽🇵🇸 <u>NINE CITIES MARCH AGAINST CHIHUAHUA’S WATER DEAL WITH ISRAEL</u>

Marches in at least nine Mexican cities — Chihuahua, Ciudad Juárez, Mexico City, Puebla, Aguascalientes, Saltillo, Pachuca, Toluca, Monterrey, Querétaro — demanded the cancellation of the water cooperation deal between Chihuahua’s water utility (JCAS) and Mashav, the Israeli Foreign Ministry’s cooperation agency, signed in February 2023 and in force until 2027.

Organizers Salvemos los Cerros and Asamblea Feminista accused PAN governor Maru Campos of promoting Zionism as "a colonial political project" and doing business with a government committing genocide in Gaza. Protesters also demanded a ceasefire and the end of Mexico-Israel diplomatic and trade ties. In Puebla, police blocked 150 marchers from reaching the Zócalo.
banner: MEXICO: 9 CITIES VS ISRAEL WATER DEAL
